correctness.rationale: For every fixed c>0 and integer ell>=2, n>ell, and independent real standard-Gaussian sketches, the finite projector identity follows by Sherman-Morrison and a direct Gaussian Schur complement of a Wishart Gram matrix with chi-squared n-ell residual degrees of freedom. For the iterative statement, the l-by-l Gram/n converges to I+cgg^T and the initial coefficient Z^TY/n converges to cgh, exactly on the unique top eigenvector. The transverse/top ratio after any positive integer power is bounded uniformly by its initial vanishing ratio because all eigenvalues are positive and the largest is simple. The map Z has condition number O_p(1) on its column coordinates, so its normalized image inherits this uniform convergence. The baseline depends on independent chi-square one; the numerator difference has a continuous joint law, justifying the beta-tail comparison. The rank-one-plus-identity decomposition of AA^T proves the spectral residual bound and bounded-convergence of expectations. The actual CHECK.py in this row passed 240 projector Schur tests, 960 direct-versus-reduced iterate tests, 960 spectral residual bounds, and 280 finite-dimension trials. Computations supplement, not establish, the uniform q claim.

originality.rationale: The novelty assessed is the uniform-over-all-positive-powers asymptotic saturation for the independently initialized sketch-power algorithm and the exact joint Gaussian capture/regression law; standard beta and inverse-Wishart ingredients are explicitly not claimed new. Chang-Yang define precisely this operator and prove general error bounds, but their q=1 near-saturation is an empirical observation, not this fixed-width chi-square crossover. Chenakkod-Derezinski consider powers of a sketch with initialization already in its range, and bounds conditional on regularized spectral approximation; the independent initial sketch and its samplewise regression probability are not treated. The other inspected mathematical results involve different operators. Semantic search cannot certify global uniqueness, but no inspected primary text yields a theorem implying this complete statement.
residual_risks: Semantic searches and inspected sources cannot establish universal bibliographic uniqueness; older spiked-Wishart or statistical PCA literature may present an equivalent independent-sketch joint limit under different terms.

The theorem is only for fixed auxiliary width, one critically scaled spike, two independent real-Gaussian sketches and exact arithmetic; no claim of general algorithmic monotonicity or oblique estimator accuracy.

value.rationale: At spike singular-value scale sqrt(c n), a fixed-width Gaussian rangefinder has an irreducible, nontrivial random capture ceiling. Knowing that even arbitrarily many additional powers cannot improve the asymptotic capture beyond q=1 is useful for deciding algorithmic iteration budgets versus sketch width. The sharp 1-1/sqrt(2) probability that an independent two-column auxiliary sketch *harms* a particular run distinguishes mean error improvements from sample-level guarantees. This is a meaningful phase-scale calculation and a structural diagnostic for one-pass low-rank algorithms, not merely a chi-square-table rewrite; it also identifies the precise regime and cases outside its scope.
